data.body_html:
Start your morning with a Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise 2032 – a 3-hour adventure from Puerto Banús that combines wild dolphin spotting with a Mediterranean brunch and cava. Priced at €749 for up to 9 guests, this is one of the most affordable private boat experiences on the Costa del Sol. The cruise runs daily from 10:00 to 13:00, taking you along the coastline from Marbella’s Golden Mile to Cabopino, where dolphins frequently feed. All aboard the Astondoa 40, a 12.5-metre flybridge with panoramic views – perfect for spotting fins.

Why choose a morning dolphin cruise?

Morning is prime time for dolphin watching in the Alboran Sea. The sea is calmer, the light is low, and dolphins are more active after night feeding. Water temperatures in summer hover around 24°C, making surface activity common. Unlike afternoon cruises, the 10:00–13:00 slot avoids the midday heat and afternoon wind (the poniente). You return to Puerto Banús by lunchtime, leaving the rest of the day free for Marbella’s beaches or the old town.

The boat: Astondoa 40

The Astondoa 40 is a Spanish-built flybridge cruiser, 12.5 metres long, with a beam of 3.8 metres. It accommodates up to 9 passengers plus a licensed skipper. The flybridge offers 360-degree views – essential for spotting dolphins. Below deck, there’s a saloon with air conditioning, a small galley, and a bathroom. The boat is equipped with a Bimini top for shade, a swim platform, and a Bluetooth sound system. Top speed: 28 knots, though dolphin-watching speed is usually 8–12 knots.

What’s included in the brunch?

The brunch is a full spread, not just nibbles. Expect a platter of fresh fruit (melon, pineapple, grapes), pastries (croissants, pain au chocolat), cured meats (jamón serrano, salchichón), cheeses (Manchego, aged goat cheese), olives, and crusty bread. Drinks include a bottle of cava, white wine, beer, soft drinks, and still/sparkling water. All are included in the €749 price. If you have dietary restrictions, let us know via WhatsApp – we can adapt the platter.

Dolphin species and best viewing spots

The most common species are bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus) and common dolphins (Delphinus delphis). Pods of 10–30 individuals are typical. The captain heads towards the Cabopino area, where a marine protected zone and seagrass meadows attract fish. Another hotspot is Cala del Faro, a rocky cove where dolphins hunt. Occasionally, you’ll see loggerhead sea turtles or shearwater seabirds. The captain uses a hydrophone to listen for clicks – a non-invasive method.

Route and timing

The cruise departs from Puerto Banús (Muelle de Honor, next to the casino). The route: head east past the Golden Mile and Marbella Marina, then towards Cabopino (about 6 NM). After dolphin watching, the boat turns back, passing Cala del Faro and the Río Verde estuary. Total distance: roughly 12–14 NM. The skipper will stop the engine for 15–20 minutes if dolphins approach, allowing you to photograph them from the bow. The return to port is at 13:00 sharp.

Pricing and availability

The Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise 2032 is priced at a flat €749 for the entire boat (up to 9 passengers). This includes skipper, fuel, insurance, brunch, drinks, and 21% VAT. There are no hidden fees. Booking is via WhatsApp only – we don’t use online calendars. Send a message with your preferred date and group size. We respond within 2 hours with availability. Payment by bank transfer or secure card link. Cancellations: free up to 48 hours before departure; after that, 50% refund.

Frequently asked questions

What time does the Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise depart?

The cruise departs at 10:00 from Puerto Banús and returns by 13:00. This morning window offers calm seas and optimal dolphin activity. We recommend arriving 15 minutes early at the marina.

How much does the dolphin watching brunch cruise cost?

The price is €749 total for the entire boat (up to 9 guests). This includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, a brunch platter, cava, soft drinks, water, beer, and white wine. Spanish VAT (21%) is included.

Will we definitely see dolphins?

We spot dolphins on approximately 90% of trips during spring and summer. Bottlenose and common dolphins are common. Sightings depend on weather and season, but the captain chooses routes to maximise chances.

What is included in the brunch?

The brunch platter includes fresh fruit, pastries, cured meats, cheese, olives, and bread. Drinks include cava, white wine, beer, soft drinks, and water. Dietary requirements can be arranged via WhatsApp.

Can children join the cruise?

Yes, children are welcome. The Astondoa 40 has a safe flybridge with railings. Life jackets for all sizes are onboard. The brunch includes kid-friendly options like juice and pastries.

What happens in bad weather?

If the captain cancels due to unsafe conditions (e.g. strong winds or high waves), you receive a full refund or can reschedule. We monitor forecasts 24 hours prior and notify you via WhatsApp.

How do I book the dolphin watching brunch cruise?

Booking is via WhatsApp only. Send a message with your preferred date and group size. We confirm availability within 2 hours. Payment is by bank transfer or card link. No online calendar.

What should I bring on the cruise?

Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, a hat, and a light jacket (morning sea breeze can be cool). A camera for dolphin shots is essential. No glass bottles – we provide all drinks.
